name: Clamp Meter
tagline: Measures current without breaking the circuit — the jaws are the transformer's core.
parts: Jaws — a split core that closes around one conductor only
Rotary dial — A~ , A⎓, volts, ohms, continuity
Zero / relative button — cancels the residual reading before a leakage test
Test leads for the voltage and continuity functions
safety: The jaws must close around ONE conductor. Clamping around a whole cable — live and neutral together — reads zero because the two currents cancel, and that zero looks exactly like a circuit that is switched off. Clamping around a single conductor of a cable also tells you nothing about the other one, so a reading taken this way is never proof that anything is dead.

points.label: Jaws (split core)
points.detail: The jaws are half of a current transformer: the conductor passing through them is a single-turn primary, and the meter reads the current induced in the core's winding. Because the coupling is magnetic there is no electrical connection at all — which is the point, since measuring amps any other way means breaking into the circuit.

points.label: Trigger
points.detail: Opens the jaws so you can close them one-handed around a conductor in a crowded board. Let it snap shut rather than easing it: a jaw that is not fully closed leaves an air gap in the magnetic circuit and reads low, sometimes by a lot.

points.label: Body and insulation
points.detail: Everything below the jaw line is a barrier as much as a housing — the jaws sit around a bare live conductor in a consumer unit, and the plastic between them and your hand is the only thing preventing a shock. Treat a cracked case the way you would treat a cracked test lead.

points.label: Display
points.detail: On AC ranges a clamp meter reads the value the transformer delivers, so the accuracy depends on the waveform: a true-RMS meter reads a dimmer or a switch-mode supply correctly, an average-responding one can be 30 % out. The reading also drifts with a small residual in the core, which is what the zero button is for.

points.label: Rotary dial
points.detail: AC and DC current, volts, resistance and continuity on one instrument. The DC ranges work on a Hall-effect sensor rather than a transformer, because a transformer cannot see DC at all — that is also the reason a clamp meter's DC current range needs zeroing before every use.

points.label: Test leads and zero button
points.detail: The leads carry the voltage, resistance and continuity functions, and must be rated for the installation category you are working in. Zero (or relative) cancels the residual reading before a leakage measurement: clamp all the live conductors of a circuit together and a healthy circuit reads very close to zero, while a fault with current escaping to earth leaves the imbalance the clamp can see.
